We can attract top faculty only if we fund strong research programs, good pay, and academic freedom; we can make college affordable only if states and the federal government are willing to invest more (Pell grants, public university funding) and if universities redirect endowment and administrative spending toward students. Practical steps: expand community-college-to-university transfer pathways, increase need-based aid, push income-driven repayment or targeted loan forgiveness for public-service grads, encourage employer tuition benefits and industry partnerships for grad research, and pressure schools to trim administrative bloat rather than cut faculty lines. Some trade-offs are unavoidable — either taxes go up or priorities shift — but with smart policy and accountability we can keep academic excellence while widening access. I’m hopeful, but it’ll take sustained effort and defending the values that make our universities magnets for talent.
